title: QUIC RFC 9000 Stream Priority Runtime Work Item
summary: Add a local stream-priority property and use it to order queued application sends in the active runtime without introducing any built-in prioritization exchange.
planned_changes:
- Add a writable-stream-local `Priority` property on `QuicStream` that round-trips through stream bookkeeping.
- Snapshot the current stream priority when application writes are queued and keep the snapshot local to the runtime.
- Sort delayed application sends by priority and preserve FIFO order for equal priorities when the queue flushes.
- Keep the wire codec, transport-parameter surface, and any built-in exchange mechanism unchanged.
- Add requirement-home coverage for the local-only priority property, priority-aware queued flush ordering, and no-wire-exchange behavior.
- Add a permanent benchmark for the priority-sorted queued-send flush path so the delayed-write hot path remains visible in the repo's performance evidence.
verification_plan: Run the focused RFC 9000 S2P3 requirement-home tests, run the new priority-sort benchmark suite, render/check the touched SpecTrace artifacts, run canonical SpecTrace JSON validation, and run `git diff --check`.
completion_notes: Implemented as a local-only stream-priority slice over the existing queued application send path, with requirement-home proof and a permanent benchmark suite covering the queue-ordering comparator.
